Definition: from the same as G5036; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with G1722 prefixed) in haste:--+ quickly, + shortly, + speedily.
BiblicalUsage: John opens Revelation with things which must shortly come to pass, and closes it the same way: the Lord sent His angel to show His servants things which must shortly be done. Jesus asks whether God will avenge His elect speedily, and then answers His own question: He will, and quickly. The word is swiftness itself, and in Revelation it carries the promise that God's purposes are not slow.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that shortly in Revelation is God's shortly, not mine. I believe His timing is sure even when it feels slow, and the repeated promise at the book's beginning and end is meant to steady us. The Judge is coming, and He will not be late.
